title: Youth Jersey Size Chart (2026)
verdict: A youth jersey size chart runs from extra small to extra large, and the right size depends on the child's measurements, not their age. This page has an example chart, a rough age guide and the steps to measure a child properly.
Kids grow during a season. When a child is between sizes, go up.

list: Chest: wrap the tape around the fullest part of the chest, level all the way round.
Waist: measure the narrowest part of the torso, above the line of the pants.
Hips: for women's or longer jerseys, measure the fullest part of the hips.
Sleeve: from the center back of the neck, over the shoulder and down to the wrist, with the arm bent.
Keep the tape snug, not tight. You should be able to slide one finger under it.
Collect measurements, not ages or T-shirt sizes.
Have players try on a sizing kit at registration.
Size up for a long season or a growing child.
Order two or three spares in YM and YL.
Tall or broad twelve-year-olds often need an adult small.

why: Wooter lists youth sizes on its jerseys in every sport and sells sizing kits, so a league can have players try on samples before it orders. Its own guide suggests re-measuring youth players every three to six months.
Order by measurement, add a size for growth, and keep a few spares in the common sizes.

faq.q: What size is a youth medium jersey?
faq.a: It varies by maker. In Wooter's baseball guide a youth medium is 23.75 inches long. A youth medium usually fits ages 8 to 10.

faq.q: What is the difference between youth XL and adult small?
faq.a: An adult small is longer and wider in the shoulders. A child at the top of the youth range often fits it better.

faq.q: Should I buy a size up for my child?
faq.a: Yes if they are between sizes or the season is long.

faq.q: Are youth sizes the same for boys and girls?
faq.a: Most youth jerseys are unisex. Some sports add girls' cuts.
Every season. Wooter's guide suggests every three to six months for growing players.
